messages.subject: CFA Model does not converge
parts:
I'm running a CFA model on data collected at separate points in time (t=3). For each point in time I run a separate CFA, but the model specification is exactly the same. The end result will be to use the factor scores of the latent variables from the CFA as control variables in a panel regression.

The model converges fine for round 1 and 3, but gives the following error for round 2:

*** WARNING *** lavaan (0.5-19) did NOT converge after 380 iterations

How can I get the model to converge? The standard answer I find is to change the specification of the model, but I don't have a lot of leeway for changing my model (given below) because I don't have any variables that can be added , and I understood that at least one variable per latent variable is required. Is it even necessary to run this model separately for each round, or can I run it in one go?


Model:
    cfa.controls <- "
        INCOME_FLOW =~ is_bshlhrvst  + is_hrswrk
        INCOME_STOCK=~  is_tin +  is_mobile
        SOCAP =~ is_youshare + is_theyshare +  is_pplhnst
        PUBGOODS =~  is_meetyn + is_work_cp + is_no_mtngs
        CONFLICT =~  is_plv_ohh + is_plv_ownhh + is_plv_lead + is_fights
        CHIEF =~     is_hlpchf + is_chf_trust + is_chf_openmny
        "
    fit.cfa.controls<- cfa(cfa.controls, data=MyData, ordered=c("is_tin", "is_mobile","is_pplhnst", "is_meetyn", "is_chf_trust", "is_chf_openmny" ))

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: CFA Model does not converge
parts:
Look at the results you are getting right now for wave 2--you can still do that, using the summary function, even though you don't have convergence.  That might help you to localize the problem.  You are more likely to find a problem where a factor has few indicators, because then, you may find your self with a "nearly not identified" kind of problem. 
     Look at your data for the second wave.  There might be an odd distribution, which could point to coding or data handling errors that you can resolve.  Is there one variable with a remarkably high (or low) variance?  Items with variances that differ by an order of magnitude can cause problems for SEM software--and are probably highly unexpected in a single wave of a multiwave study.  In the correlation matrix, is there a variable with a very small correlation with other variable which are supposedly indicators of the same common factor?  Are you handling missing data the same way, and is missing data perhaps more prevalent in wave 2?
     Set starting values for the parameter estimates close to the final values you expect.  Since you have results for 2 waves of data, you might loo at those values.  You want to keep loadings and factor correlations away from 0--so start them with the right sign, with minimum values of, say, +/- 0.5, assuming your sample size are reasonable.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: Re: CFA Model does not converge
parts: Thank you for your comprehensive suggestions! By providing starting valuesI found out what factor was causing the problem. It turned out that two variables that loaded on one factor were very weakly correlated. When I dropped that factor from the model it ran without problems.
